sortieLongue.note: Easy pace, steady from start to finish. Stay hydrated.

lignesDroites.note: 40 min easy, then 5 progressive 100 m strides, walking back.

vma400.note: 20 min easy warm-up + drills. Jog recoveries.

trenteTrente.note: 2 sets of 10 × 30 s fast / 30 s easy, 3 min recovery between sets.

pyramide.note: Recovery = same time as the effort, jogging.

cotes.note: Moderate slope, powerful uphill, jog down to recover.

programmes.intro: Choose a program: the app suggests the right workout every time, with your weights from last time.

full3.desc: Your whole body every workout, 3 times a week. Ideal for starting out or getting back into it.
full3.conseil: Add a little weight as soon as you complete all your sets with good form.

ppl.desc: The great classic: push, pull, legs. 3 workouts a week (or 6 if you run it twice).
ppl.conseil: Keep 1 to 2 reps in reserve (RPE 8) on most sets.

upper4.desc: 4 workouts: 2 upper body, 2 lower body. Perfect for building mass.
upper4.conseil: Workout A heavy (few reps), workout B lighter (more reps).

force5.desc: Few exercises, lots of strength: 5 sets of 5 on the big lifts, alternating 2 workouts.
force5.conseil: Add 2.5 kg after every successful workout (5 kg on the deadlift). If you fail 3 times, drop 10%.

calis1.desc: Bodyweight, no gym: the basics for your first pull-ups and dips.
calis1.conseil: When you get through all the sets easily, move to the harder variation (e.g. push-ups → diamond push-ups).

run10.desc: 8 weeks to run 10K: one easy run, one speed session and one long run a week.
run10.conseil: Keep the easy run and the long run conversational: you should be able to talk.

formatsAide.fortime: Finish the work as fast as possible. Your score = your time.
formatsAide.amrap: “As Many Rounds As Possible” in the time given.

bench.helen: 3 rounds: 400 m run, 21 KB swings (24/16 kg), 12 pull-ups
bench.cindy: AMRAP 20 min: 5 Pull-ups, 10 Push-ups, 15 Air squats

crossfit.nomWodExemple: e.g. Fran, Murph, WOD of the day

fran.rx: 43 kg bar for men, 29 kg for women.
fran.scaled: 20 or 15 kg bar, banded pull-ups or ring rows.
fran.tip: Break up the pull-ups from the first round (e.g. 11 + 10) so you don’t blow up your forearms.

etapes.e1: 30 clean & jerks, however you like: unbroken, in sets or one at a time

grace.rx: 61 kg bar for men, 43 kg for women.
grace.scaled: A weight you can lift 10 times in a row without straining (e.g. 40 / 25 kg).
grace.tip: Do steady singles (one rep every 5 to 10 s) rather than big sets that wreck you.

etapes.e1: 30 snatches, bar from the floor to overhead in one movement

isabel.rx: 61 kg bar for men, 43 kg for women.
isabel.scaled: Light power snatch (e.g. 35 / 25 kg) or alternating dumbbell snatch.
isabel.tip: Like Grace: fast singles, keeping your back braced on every rep.

diane.rx: 102 kg bar for men, 70 kg for women. Handstand push-ups against the wall.
diane.scaled: 60 / 40 kg bar, pike push-ups or dumbbell overhead press.
diane.tip: The deadlifts go fast: save energy for the handstand push-ups, broken into small sets.

elizabeth.rx: 61 kg bar for men, 43 kg for women.
elizabeth.scaled: Lighter bar (40 / 25 kg), bar or bench dips.
elizabeth.tip: Link the cleans touch-and-go as long as your technique holds, then switch to singles.

helen.rx: 24 kg kettlebell for men, 16 kg for women. Overhead swings.
helen.tip: Recover on the run without slowing down: that’s where you gain time by going straight into the swings.

etapes.e1: 150 wall balls: full squat with the medicine ball, then throw it to the target

karen.rx: 9 kg ball to 3 m for men, 6 kg to 2.70 m for women.
karen.scaled: Lighter ball (6 / 4 kg) or a lower target.
karen.tip: Set your sets from the start (e.g. 15 reps then 3 breaths), before you get tired.

annie.rx: Double unders: the rope passes under your feet twice on each jump.
annie.scaled: Single unders (twice as many jumps) or fewer reps.
annie.tip: Keep a steady rhythm on the sit-ups: they’re what slows you down most at the end of the WOD.

jackie.rx: 20 kg bar for men, 15 kg for women.
jackie.scaled: A lighter empty bar, banded pull-ups or ring rows.
jackie.tip: Don’t start too fast on the rower: your breathing needs to be ready for the 50 thrusters.

etapes.e4: Repeat as many rounds as possible in 20 minutes

cindy.rx: Bodyweight. Chest-to-floor push-ups, squats below parallel.
cindy.scaled: Banded pull-ups, knee push-ups or hands elevated.
cindy.tip: Keep a steady pace, about one round per minute, rather than starting too fast.
cindy.score: Your score: the number of full rounds + the reps of the round in progress.

etapes.e2: 100 pull-ups, 200 push-ups, 300 air squats (split them however you like, e.g. 20 rounds of 5-10-15)

murph.rx: Wearing a 9 kg weighted vest for men, 6 kg for women.
murph.scaled: No vest, half the reps (“half Murph”) or banded pull-ups.
murph.tip: Split it into 20 rounds of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, 15 squats: it’s the easiest way to get through.

how.chrono: The clock starts on “3, 2, 1, go” and stops on the last rep. Your score is your time.

commentFaire.q: How do I learn to do an exercise?
commentFaire.mots: how to do exercise movement technique form animation figure help perform
commentFaire.r:
Tap the little red “?”: in your workout next to the exercise name, or right in the exercise search (without adding it).
The movement is animated from the side and the front (start then finish, on a loop), with a technique tip and, for push-ups, presses and pull-ups, a diagram of hand placement.
The working muscles are shown in red.

boutonGo.mots: lets go let go start begin workout home plus button bar
boutonGo.r:
The big + button in the middle of the bottom bar opens today’s workout directly.
The “Workouts” tab brings together free workouts (calendar), your routines, programs and workout ideas. Home shows your muscle map, progress, trophies, PRs and recap.

creerRoutine.q: How do I create a routine?
creerRoutine.mots: routine save template repeat workout favorite
creerRoutine.r:
Two ways:
• in a workout, tap “☆ Save as routine”;
• or Workouts › My routines › “+ Create a routine”.
Then one tap on “Start” and the workout is ready, with your weights from last time.

suivreProgramme.q: How do I follow a program?
suivreProgramme.mots: program plan weeks ppl full body 5x5 10k training follow
suivreProgramme.r:
Workouts › Programs, then “Follow this program”.
The app then suggests the right workout each time (“▶ Start”), week after week.

derniereFois.mots: last time history previous weight prefilled before
derniereFois.r: When you add an exercise you’ve done before, the app shows what you did last time (↺) and reuses your weights. Reps are suggested in gray: type yours or confirm the set.

recordsDirect.mots: record new pr personal best beat trophy live
recordsDirect.r: When you complete a set heavier than your best (or more reps at the same weight), a “New PR!” message appears, with confetti. For running: your longest run and your best pace. Your friends see your PRs in the feed.

serie.mots: streak flame goal week weekly ring
serie.r: On Home, choose your goal of workouts per week (tap the ring). Every week you hit it grows your 🔥 streak. “Rest” days don’t count.

plusieursSeances.q: Several workouts on the same day?
plusieursSeances.mots: several two workouts same day morning evening double
plusieursSeances.r: Yes: in a workout, tap “+ Another workout” at the top, or “+ New” in Workouts. The day’s workouts show up as tabs.

carteMusculaire.mots: muscle map muscles body worked forgotten
carteMusculaire.r: Home › Muscle map: the muscles worked over 7 or 30 days light up, from lightest to reddest. Tap a muscle to see how many sets it got.

partagerBilan.q: How do I share my recap?
partagerBilan.mots: recap month story share instagram image summary
partagerBilan.r: Home › Monthly recap, then “📲 Share as a story”. An image is created with your numbers for the month: share it on Insta, Snap or WhatsApp.

cordes.q: How do I log a rope workout?
cordes.mots: rope ropes climb rope climb set start weight
cordes.r:
Tap a day, then choose “Ropes”. For each exercise: number of climbs, a new set every X seconds or minutes, with or without added weight.
“⏱ Start the sets” makes the timer ring at each set.

defi.q: How do I start a challenge?
defi.r: Social › Challenges › “+ New challenge”: choose what counts (workouts, active days, km or volume), the duration and the friends you invite. The leaderboard updates automatically.

commenter.q: How do I comment on a workout?
commenter.r: Social: in the feed, under each of your friends’ workouts, write your comment and tap “Send”. You see comments on your workouts in Social and on the workout itself.

noterSeance.q: How do I log a workout?
noterSeance.mots: log workout add training day calendar create
noterSeance.r:
Go to Workouts, then tap the day you want in the calendar (or “Log today’s workout”).
Choose your activity: Strength training, CrossFit, Calisthenics or Running. Each activity has its own tailored log.

ajouterSeries.mots: set sets reps repetitions weight kg exercise add
ajouterSeries.r:
In your workout, tap “+ Add an exercise”, type its name, then fill in Reps and Weight for each set.
“+ Add a set” copies the previous set to save time.

repos.mots: rest timer stopwatch time break recovery
repos.r:
Under each exercise, set your rest time with − and + (in 15 s steps).
After your set, tap “✓ Set 1 done · rest”: the set turns green and the timer starts. When the rest is over, the next set lights up on its own. “+15 s” adds time, “Skip” goes straight to the next set.

enregistrement.mots: save saved backup lost lose button confirm
enregistrement.r:
Yes, everything saves automatically as you type, no button needed.
A red message appears at the top only if there’s a connection problem.

rpe.r:
RPE rates difficulty from 1 to 10.
8 = you had 2 reps left in the tank, 9 = 1 rep, 10 = failure. It helps you know when to increase the weight.

photo.q: How do I add a photo?
photo.r:
Open your workout and scroll down to “Photos”, then tap “+ Take a photo”.
Tap a photo to enlarge or delete it.

reprendre.q: How do I repeat my last workout?
reprendre.r: On an empty day, choose the workout type: a “Repeat last workout” button appears. It copies your exercises and weights.

types.q: How do I change types and colors?
types.mots: type color edit push pull legs cardio ropes rest
types.r: In Workouts, tap the “Types” button. You can rename a type, change its color (tap the dot), add or remove types.

creatine.q: How do I log my creatine?
creatine.r:
Nutrition › Creatine: tap the big circle, it turns red = taken.
Forgot a day? Tap the date in the calendar below. The dose is set at the bottom of the page.

complement.q: How do I add a supplement?
complement.mots: supplement whey protein omega vitamin magnesium
complement.r: Nutrition › Supplements: tap a supplement in “Quick add”, or type a new one with its dose. The arrows at the top change the day.

installer.q: How do I install the app on my phone?
installer.mots: install app application home screen download icon
installer.r:
On iPhone: in Safari, tap Share then “Add to Home Screen”.
On Android: ⋮ menu then “Install app”.
There’s also a button in your Profile.

modifierProfil.q: How do I edit my profile?
modifierProfil.mots: profile edit photo username weight height age goal info
modifierProfil.r: Tap “You” at the bottom right, then “Edit profile”. Change whatever you want and tap “Save”.

motDePasse.mots: password forgot forgotten reset login log in
motDePasse.r: On the login screen, type your email then tap “Forgot your password?”. You’ll get a link by email (check your spam folder too).

donneesPrivees.r:
Other users can’t see your data.
The app’s administrator can view accounts to manage the app and help you.

horsConnexion.r: Yes, the app opens without a connection and keeps your changes. They’re sent as soon as you’re back online.

supprimerCompte.q: How do I delete my account?
supprimerCompte.r: You › “Delete my account and data”, then confirm with your password. Everything is permanently erased.

course.q: How do I log a run?
course.mots: run running jog jogging easy run tempo intervals vo2 pace distance km
course.r:
Tap a day › Running, then choose Easy run, Tempo or Intervals.
Enter the distance and time: your pace (min/km) and speed are calculated automatically. For tempo and interval runs, add your blocks (e.g. 10 × 400 m, 1:00 recovery) and start the recovery timer.

wod.q: How do I log a CrossFit WOD?
wod.r:
Tap a day › CrossFit. Choose the format (For Time, AMRAP, EMOM…), write the movements, then your score and Rx or Scaled.
Type “Fran”, “Murph”… in the WOD name: the movements fill in automatically.

recordsCrossfit.q: Where do I see my CrossFit PRs?
recordsCrossfit.mots: record 1rm pr max load benchmark girls fran murph cindy
recordsCrossfit.r: On Home, tap CrossFit: that’s where you log your PRs (1RM) in back squat, clean, snatch… and your times on benchmark WODs like Fran or Murph.

calis.q: How do I log a calisthenics workout?
calis.mots: calisthenics street workout pull up dips muscle front lever planche handstand bodyweight
calis.r: Tap a day › Calisthenics. Add your exercises in one tap (Pull-ups, Dips, Front lever…). For held skills, tap “Reps ⇄” to log seconds. The Added weight column is for when you go weighted.

idees.q: Where can I find workout ideas?
idees.mots: idea ideas workout type program example inspiration try
idees.r:
On Home, tap “Workout ideas” then choose your activity: Strength training (Push, Pull, Legs…), CrossFit, Calisthenics or Running.
Each idea has a “Try today” button that fills in today’s workout.

recordsPR.q: Where do I log my PRs?
recordsPR.mots: record pr 5k 10k half marathon bench press squat deadlift
recordsPR.r: Home › PRs, then choose your category: Strength training, CrossFit, Calisthenics or Running. Tap + to add a PR: your best shows up in big numbers.

progression.q: Where can I see my progress?
progression.mots: progress chart graph curve evolution stats statistics
progression.r: Home › Progress, then choose your category. In strength training, choose Push, Pull…: each exercise has its own chart with your max weight for every workout. Tap a chart to see a workout’s value.

son.q: How do I set the timer sound?
son.mots: sound volume timer stopwatch beep alarm hear loud
son.r:
You › “Timer sound”: set the volume, choose Beep, Alarm, Whistle or Gong, and tap “Test the sound”.
On iPhone, there’s no sound when the silent switch (on the side) is on.

serieCouleur.r: In a workout, the set you’re on is outlined in your main color (“Current set”). Fill in your reps and weight, then tap “✓ Set done”: it turns green, the rest starts, and the next one lights up when the timer ends.

ajouterAmi.q: How do I add a friend?
ajouterAmi.mots: friend friends add code username request accept
ajouterAmi.r: Social › Friends (or the 🔍 magnifier). Show your QR code (You › Share) or give your friend code (e.g. THEO-4821) to your buddies, or search for their code or username, then tap “Add”. Your friend accepts the request and you’re done.

messageAmi.q: How do I message a friend?
messageAmi.mots: message messages write chat conversation talk
messageAmi.r: Social › 💬 at the top right, or Friends then tap 💬 next to your friend. Messages are only visible to the two of you. A red dot shows new messages.

essayerSeanceAmi.q: How do I try a friend’s workout?
essayerSeanceAmi.mots: workout friend try copy follow see
essayerSeanceAmi.r: Social › Friends, tap your friend then one of their workouts, and “Try this workout”: it’s copied into today’s workout, with their weights as a target. You can also react with 💪 🔥 👏.

quiVoit.mots: see workouts private share sharing privacy friends
quiVoit.r: Only your accepted friends, and only if “Share my workouts with my friends” is on (Social › Friends). Your nutrition and personal info are never shared.

bloquer.q: How do I block or report someone?
bloquer.r: In a conversation, tap ••• then “Block” or “Report”. You can also tap a message to report it. Reports go to the administrator.

contacter.q: How do I contact the creator?
contacter.mots: contact creator problem bug help complaint idea
contacter.r: Tap “Contact” at the bottom of Home, choose a subject and write your message: it comes straight to me.

3030.r: 30/30 = 30 seconds fast (around your vVO2max) then 30 seconds easy, repeated (e.g. 2 × 10 times). It’s a classic short interval session.

21159.r:
It’s a rep scheme: 21 of each movement, then 15, then 9.
E.g. Fran: 21 thrusters, 21 pull-ups, 15 thrusters, 15 pull-ups, 9 thrusters, 9 pull-ups.

wod.r:
WOD = “Workout Of the Day”.
In CrossFit, it’s the main part of the class: often short (5 to 20 min) and intense, mixing cardio, gymnastics and weightlifting.

rx.q: What do Rx and Scaled mean?
rx.r:
Rx (“as prescribed”) = you do the WOD exactly as written: official loads, movements and reps.
Scaled = a version adapted to your level: lighter weight, banded pull-ups, knee push-ups…
There’s no shame in going Scaled: that’s how you progress without getting hurt.

fortime.mots: for time clock fast possible time
fortime.r:
For Time = you do all the work as fast as possible. Your score is your time.
There’s often a “time cap” (maximum time).

timecap.r:
The time cap is the maximum time allowed for a WOD.
If you haven’t finished in time, your score = the number of reps completed (written e.g. “CAP + 12”).

amrap.mots: amrap many rounds possible max rounds
amrap.r:
AMRAP = “As Many Rounds As Possible” in a given time.
E.g. AMRAP 12 min of 5 pull-ups, 10 push-ups, 15 squats. You keep going round after round until the beep.
Score = full rounds + reps of the round in progress (e.g. 8 rounds + 7).

emom.r:
EMOM = “Every Minute On the Minute”: at the start of each minute, you do the work, then rest for the rest of the minute.
E.g. EMOM 10 min: 3 power cleans. The faster you go, the more you rest.
An “E2MOM” = every 2 minutes.

tabata.r:
Tabata = 8 rounds of 20 seconds all-out / 10 seconds rest, so 4 minutes.
Score: total reps, or your weakest round, depending on the instructions.

chipper.r:
A Chipper is a long list of high-rep movements, done just once, in order.
You “chip away” at them little by little. E.g. 50 box jumps, 50 wall balls, 50 burpees…

1rm.q: What are a 1RM and a PR?
1rm.mots: 1rm rm pr personal record max load rep
1rm.r:
1RM = “1 Repetition Max”: the heaviest weight you can lift once.
PR = “Personal Record”, your personal best. Log them in the CrossFit tab to track your progress.

girls.q: What are the Girls and Hero WODs?
girls.mots: girls hero benchmark reference fran murph grace cindy
girls.r:
They’re benchmark WODs, always the same, to measure your progress.
The “Girls” have women’s names (Fran, Grace, Cindy…). The “Hero WODs” honor soldiers or firefighters who died in the line of duty (Murph…).
You’ll find them all in the CrossFit tab.

charges.mots: load men women slash two weights
charges.r:
Two loads separated by “/” = men’s load / women’s load.
E.g. Thrusters 43/29 kg: 43 kg for men, 29 kg for women (Rx version).

metcon.r: Metcon = “metabolic conditioning”: the intense, cardio part of the WOD that gets your heart rate up (often a For Time or an AMRAP).

kipping.q: Kipping or strict, what’s the difference?
kipping.mots: kipping strict swing momentum pull up
kipping.r:
Strict = a movement with no momentum (e.g. a strict pull-up).
Kipping = you use a body swing to link reps faster (pull-ups, toes to bar, HSPU). “Butterfly” is an even faster kipping style.

unbroken.r: Unbroken = all the reps of a set without stopping or dropping the bar.

thruster.r: A thruster = a front squat linked with an overhead press in one fluid movement: you use the drive out of the squat to push the bar up.

wallball.mots: wall ball medicine ball wall target
wallball.r: Wall ball = a squat holding a medicine ball at your chest, then you throw the ball to a target on the wall (3 m for men, 2.70 m for women) and catch it.

doubleunder.r: Double under = with a jump rope, the rope passes under your feet twice in a single jump.

t2b.mots: toes to bar feet bar hanging abs
t2b.r: Toes to bar = hanging from the bar, you raise your feet until they touch the bar.

muscleup.mots: muscle up rings bar pull up dips
muscleup.r: Muscle-up = a pull-up linked with a dip to get your chest above the bar or rings. It’s an advanced movement.

hspu.r: HSPU = “Handstand Push-Up”: a push-up in a handstand, feet against the wall.

halterophilie.q: Clean, snatch, jerk: what are they?
halterophilie.r:
They’re the Olympic weightlifting movements:
• Clean: the bar goes from the floor to your shoulders.
• Jerk: from your shoulders to overhead.
• Clean & jerk: both linked.
• Snatch: from the floor to overhead in one movement.
“Power” = catching in a half squat instead of a full squat.

kbswing.r: KB swing = you swing a kettlebell between your legs then up to eye level (Russian swing) or overhead (American swing), driven by your hips.

burpee.r: Burpee = you drop your chest to the floor, get back up and jump, clapping your hands overhead.

ef.mots: easy run base zone 2 slow jog aerobic
ef.r:
An easy run is a slow, comfortable pace: you can talk while running. About 60 to 75% of your max heart rate.
It makes up most of a runner’s training: it builds your “engine” without wearing you out.

seuil.r:
Threshold is a comfortably hard pace that you could hold for about 45 min to 1 hour in a race. About 85 to 90% of your max HR.
In training, you work on it in blocks (e.g. 3 × 10 min at threshold, 2 min recovery).

fractionne.r:
Intervals alternate fast efforts and recoveries.
E.g. 10 × 400 m fast with 1 min recovery, or 30/30. That’s what improves your speed and VO2 max.

vma.r:
vVO2max (called VMA in French) = Maximal Aerobic Speed: the speed at which you use the most oxygen. You can hold it for about 4 to 7 minutes.
It’s used to set interval paces (e.g. 30/30 at 100% of vVO2max).

allure.r:
Pace is the time it takes to cover 1 km (e.g. 5:00 /km).
5:00 /km = 12 km/h, 6:00 /km = 10 km/h, 4:00 /km = 15 km/h. The app works it out for you from your distance and time.

fc.r:
Max HR is your maximum heart rate (in beats per minute). A simple estimate: 220 − your age, but it varies a lot from person to person.
Your run’s average HR is on your watch.

notes.murph: You can split the pull-ups, push-ups and squats however you like (e.g. 20 rounds of 5-10-15), but the run is done at the start and the end.
notes.cindy: Keep cycling rounds without stopping for 20 minutes: your score = rounds + reps.
notes.fran: It’s one of the best-known WODs: very short (often 3 to 10 min) but very intense.
notes.helen: Go through it 3 times: the run, the swings, then the pull-ups.
notes.annie: 50 double unders and 50 sit-ups, then 40 and 40, and so on down to 10.

crunch-a-la-poulie.consigne: Kneeling facing the high pulley, rope held behind your head: curl your back toward the floor by squeezing your abs, then come back up slowly.
crunch-a-la-poulie.conseil1: Your hips stay above your knees and don’t move.
crunch-a-la-poulie.conseil2: Hands fixed against your head: it’s your back that curls.
crunch-a-la-poulie.conseil3: Breathe out on the way down.

crunch.legende2: Upper back curled, lower back on the floor
crunch.consigne: Lying on your back, knees bent and feet flat: curl your upper back as you breathe out, without pulling on your neck, then lower back down.
crunch.conseil1: Feet flat on the floor, heels close to your glutes.
crunch.conseil2: Your lower back stays on the floor: only your shoulders lift.
crunch.conseil3: Hands against your temples, without pulling on your head.

gainage-lateral.consigne: On one forearm, elbow under your shoulder: body in a straight line from head to feet, without letting your hips drop or rise.
gainage-lateral.conseil2: Body in line: your hips don’t rise or sag.
gainage-lateral.conseil3: Too hard? Put your bottom knee on the floor.

gainage.consigne: On your forearms, elbows under your shoulders, forearms pointing forward: body in a straight line from shoulders to heels.
gainage.conseil1: Elbows under your shoulders, forearms parallel and pointing forward.
gainage.conseil2: Body straight: no butt in the air, no sagging belly.
gainage.conseil3: Squeeze your abs and glutes, breathe normally.

hollow-hold.consigne: Lying on your back, lower back pressed into the floor: arms straight behind your head and legs straight, both lifted off the floor.
hollow-hold.conseil1: Your lower back stays on the floor.
hollow-hold.conseil2: Shoulders and feet a few centimeters off the floor.
hollow-hold.conseil3: Too hard? Bend your knees or keep your arms by your sides.

mountain-climbers.consigne: In a high plank, arms straight: drive one knee toward your chest, then the other, alternating fast without lifting your hips.
mountain-climbers.conseil1: One knee after the other, never both at once.
mountain-climbers.conseil2: Hands under your shoulders, arms straight.

releves-de-jambes.consigne: Hanging from the bar without swinging: raise your straight legs to horizontal, then lower them slowly.
releves-de-jambes.conseil2: No momentum: your legs go up and down slowly.
releves-de-jambes.conseil3: Too hard? Raise your knees bent.

roue-abdominale.consigne: Kneeling, hands on the wheel under your shoulders: roll forward keeping your back flat, then come back by squeezing your abs.
roue-abdominale.conseil1: Back flat, glutes tight: your lower back never arches.
roue-abdominale.conseil2: Don’t go further than you can control.
roue-abdominale.conseil3: Beginner: short range of motion, or roll toward a wall.

russian-twist.consigne: Seated, torso leaning back as at the top of a crunch, feet off the floor: move the weight from side to side by rotating your shoulders.
russian-twist.conseil1: Back straight (not rounded), torso leaning at about 45°.
russian-twist.conseil2: Your shoulders rotate, the weight follows.
russian-twist.conseil3: Too hard? Keep your heels on the floor.

sit-ups.legende2: Torso raised up to your knees
sit-ups.consigne: Lying down, knees bent, feet flat (anchored if needed): raise your whole torso up to your knees, then lower back down gently.
sit-ups.conseil1: Feet flat, toes forward, tucked under a support if needed.
sit-ups.conseil2: Roll up through your back on the way up, lower slowly.
sit-ups.conseil3: Hands against your temples or arms crossed over your chest.

toes-to-bar.consigne: Hanging from the bar: raise your feet until they touch the bar, legs straight, then lower them under control.
toes-to-bar.conseil1: Your toes touch the bar, between your hands.
toes-to-bar.conseil3: Control the descent so you don’t swing.

communs-bras.consigne: Elbows tucked in, thumbs up: curl the dumbbells up without swinging, then lower them slowly.
communs-bras.conseil1: Hammer grip: thumbs up throughout the movement.
communs-bras.conseil3: No momentum: if you swing, go lighter.

barre-au-front.consigne: Lying on a bench, bar held with arms straight above your face: bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten your arms.
barre-au-front.conseil1: Hands shoulder-width apart (straight or EZ bar).
barre-au-front.conseil2: Your elbows stay fixed, pointing at the ceiling.
barre-au-front.conseil3: Lower slowly toward your forehead, without touching it.

curl-a-la-poulie.consigne: Facing the low pulley, bar in hand: curl the bar toward your shoulders keeping your elbows fixed, then lower it slowly.
curl-a-la-poulie.conseil1: Take a step back so the cable stays taut at the bottom.
curl-a-la-poulie.conseil3: Cable tension stays constant: lower slowly.

curl-barre.legende2: Bar at your shoulders, elbows fixed
curl-barre.consigne: EZ bar in hand, palms facing forward, elbows tucked in: curl the bar up without swinging, then lower it slowly.
curl-barre.conseil1: EZ (cambered) bar: easier on the wrists.
curl-barre.conseil2: Only your forearms move, your elbows stay at your sides.

curl-halteres.consigne: Dumbbells at your sides, palms facing your thighs: curl up while turning your wrists so your palms finish facing your shoulders, then lower while turning back.
curl-halteres.conseil1: Supination: your wrist turns on the way up (palms up at the top).
curl-halteres.conseil3: Go up and down slowly, without momentum.

curl-incline.consigne: Seated on an incline bench, arms hanging behind your torso: curl the dumbbells up without bringing your elbows forward, then lower slowly.
curl-incline.conseil1: Bench at 45–60°, back and head against the backrest.
curl-incline.conseil2: Arms vertical at the start, behind your torso: your elbows don’t move.
curl-incline.conseil3: Lighter weight than a standing curl.

curl-poignets.consigne: Seated, forearms resting on your thighs, wrists over the edge, palms up: curl your wrists up, then lower them.
curl-poignets.conseil1: Forearms flat on your thighs, wrists past your knees.

curl-pupitre.legende1: Arms almost straight on the pad
curl-pupitre.consigne: Seated, backs of your arms on the preacher pad: curl the bar toward your shoulders, then lower slowly without snapping your arms straight.
curl-pupitre.conseil1: Armpits snug at the top of the pad.
curl-pupitre.conseil2: The backs of your arms stay on the pad.
curl-pupitre.conseil3: Keep a slight bend in your elbows at the bottom.

extension-triceps-a-la-poulie.consigne: Facing the high pulley, elbows tucked in: push your arms fully straight down, then come back up under control.
extension-triceps-a-la-poulie.conseil2: Fully straighten your arms at the bottom.
extension-triceps-a-la-poulie.conseil3: Come back up slowly until your forearms are horizontal.

extension-triceps-nuque.consigne: Dumbbell held in both hands overhead: lower it behind your neck by bending your elbows, then straighten your arms upward.
extension-triceps-nuque.conseil1: Elbows pointing up, close to your head.
extension-triceps-nuque.conseil3: Abs tight so you don’t arch (or sit with your back supported).

kickback-triceps.consigne: One knee and one hand on a bench, back flat, upper arm against your body: extend your forearm backward, then return slowly.
kickback-triceps.conseil1: Knee and hand on the same side on the bench, back parallel to the floor.
kickback-triceps.conseil2: Your upper arm stays against your body and doesn’t move.

communs-calisthenie.conseil1: Start with your arms fully straight, shoulders down.
communs-calisthenie.conseil2: Head straight, eyes forward: your chest rises to the bar, your head doesn’t go under it.
communs-calisthenie.conseil3: Drive your elbows down and back, without swinging your legs.
communs-calisthenie.conseil4: Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

back-lever.consigne: Hanging, arms straight behind your back: body tight and horizontal, face down.
back-lever.conseil1: Face down, body straight from shoulders to feet.
back-lever.conseil3: Progression: tucked legs, then one leg straight.

dips-aux-anneaux.consigne: Rings held with arms straight close to your body: lower until your elbows are at 90°, then push back up keeping the rings tight.
dips-aux-anneaux.conseil1: Less stable than bars: master regular dips first.
dips-aux-anneaux.conseil2: Rings against your body, arms straight at the top.
dips-aux-anneaux.conseil3: Lower slowly without letting the rings drift apart.

dips.consigne: Hands gripping the bars, arms straight: lower until your elbows are at 90°, then push back up.
dips.conseil1: Hands wrapped around the bars, wrists straight.
dips.conseil2: Shoulders down, away from your ears.
dips.conseil3: Torso leaning forward = more chest; torso upright = more triceps.

front-lever.consigne: Hanging with arms straight: body tight and horizontal, face up.
front-lever.conseil1: Arms straight, pull the bar toward your hips.
front-lever.conseil2: Body straight: no sagging hips, no arched back.
front-lever.conseil3: Progression: tucked knees, then one leg straight.

handstand-push-up.consigne: In a handstand, feet against the wall: lower your head close to the floor by bending your arms, then press back up to straight arms.
handstand-push-up.conseil1: Hands 20–30 cm from the wall, shoulder-width apart.
handstand-push-up.conseil2: Lower slowly, your head just brushes the floor.
handstand-push-up.conseil3: Progression: pike push-ups on a bench.

handstand.consigne: Hands shoulder-width apart, body tight and stacked, eyes between your hands.
handstand.conseil1: Start against a wall, facing the wall.
handstand.conseil3: Body stacked: hands, shoulders, hips, feet.

human-flag.consigne: Hands gripping a vertical pole, arms straight: top arm pulls, bottom arm pushes, body horizontal to the side.
human-flag.conseil1: Hands about one and a half shoulder-widths apart on the pole.
human-flag.conseil2: Top arm pulls, bottom arm pushes, both straight.
human-flag.conseil3: Progression: start with tucked legs, then one leg straight.

l-sit.consigne: Arms straight, supported on bars, shoulders down: legs straight and horizontal.
l-sit.conseil1: Shoulders down, away from your ears.
l-sit.conseil2: Legs together and straight, toes pointed.
l-sit.conseil3: Progression: one knee bent, then both legs straight.

montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.legende1: Hands high, feet clamping the rope
montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.legende2: Legs push, one hand then the other
montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.consigne: Hands gripping high, feet locking the rope: push with your legs, then move one hand above the other.
montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.conseil1: Your feet pinch the rope (one ankle over the other).
montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.conseil2: Your legs do the climbing, your arms hold on.
montee-de-corde-avec-jambes.conseil3: Come down hand over hand, never by sliding.

montee-de-corde-depart-assis.legende1: Seated on the floor, legs straight, hands on the rope
montee-de-corde-depart-assis.consigne: Seated on the floor, legs straight in front of you, hands on the rope: pull with your arms to lift off, then climb hand over hand without using your legs.
montee-de-corde-depart-assis.conseil1: Seated start: no leg drive to lift off.
montee-de-corde-depart-assis.conseil2: Legs straight in front of you, tight, throughout the climb.
montee-de-corde-depart-assis.conseil3: Come down hand over hand until you’re seated again.

montee-de-corde.consigne: Arms only, legs slightly raised: climb hand over hand.
montee-de-corde.conseil1: Legs raised in front of you, no swinging.
montee-de-corde.conseil2: One hand after the other, arms pulling.
montee-de-corde.conseil3: Come down hand over hand as well.

muscle-up.legende2: Explosive pull, chest to the bar
muscle-up.legende3: Body above the bar, arms straight
muscle-up.consigne: Pull explosively to your chest, roll your wrists over the bar, then press until your arms are straight, body above the bar.
muscle-up.conseil1: First master 10 strict pull-ups and some dips.
muscle-up.conseil2: Pull the bar toward your lower chest, not your chin.
muscle-up.conseil3: At the end, arms straight and hips level with the bar.

planche.legende1: Position to hold: shoulders ahead of your hands
planche.consigne: Feet-on-the-floor version (planche lean): supported on your hands, arms straight, shift your shoulders ahead of your hands while keeping your body tight.
planche.conseil1: Arms fully straight, shoulders pushing the floor away.
planche.conseil2: Fingers turned out or back to protect your wrists.
planche.conseil3: Body tight from start to finish, toes on the floor.

pompes-archer.legende2: Lower to the right, left arm straight
pompes-archer.legende3: Lower to the left, right arm straight
pompes-archer.consigne: Hands very wide: lower to one side by bending that arm while the other stays straight, push back up, then lower to the other side.
pompes-archer.conseil1: One side then the other, never both at once.
pompes-archer.conseil2: The straight arm slides out to the side and helps a little.
pompes-archer.conseil3: Body tight and straight throughout the movement.

pompes-diamant.consigne: Hands together under your chest in a diamond shape: lower keeping your elbows tight to your body, then push up.
pompes-diamant.conseil1: Thumbs and index fingers touch under your chest.
pompes-diamant.conseil2: Elbows against your body, even more than in regular push-ups.
pompes-diamant.conseil3: Harder: start on your knees if needed.

pompes-pike.legende1: Body in a V, arms straight
pompes-pike.legende2: Head toward the floor in front of your hands
pompes-pike.consigne: Hands on the floor, hips high (body in an upside-down V): bend your arms to bring your head toward the floor in front of your hands, then push.
pompes-pike.conseil1: Hips high: your body makes an upside-down V.
pompes-pike.conseil2: Your head comes down in front of your hands, not between them.
pompes-pike.conseil3: The closer your feet are to your hands, the harder it is.

pompes.consigne: Body tight in a plank, hands slightly wider than your shoulders: lower your chest close to the floor, elbows close to your body, then push.
pompes.conseil1: Elbows at about 45° from your body, not flared.
pompes.conseil2: Body straight as a plank: no butt in the air, no sagging belly.
pompes.conseil3: Too hard? Do them on your knees or with your hands on a bench.

tractions-australiennes.consigne: Under a low bar, body tight and straight, heels on the floor: pull your chest up to the bar, elbows close to your body, then lower.
tractions-australiennes.conseil1: Body straight from shoulders to heels.
tractions-australiennes.conseil2: Elbows close to your body, chest toward the bar.
tractions-australiennes.conseil3: The further away your feet are, the harder it is.

tractions-lestees.consigne: Dip belt around your hips, weight hanging between your legs: same movement as a regular pull-up.
tractions-lestees.conseil1: Belt tight on your hips, plate hanging between your legs without swinging.

tractions-supination-chin-up.consigne: Hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing you: pull your chest toward the bar, chin over, then lower.

tractions.consigne: Hanging with arms straight, hands slightly wider than your shoulders: pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it, then lower.

air-bike.consigne: Pedal and push-pull the handles at the same time: the faster you go, the more the air resists. You count in calories.
air-bike.conseil1: Set the seat: leg almost straight when the pedal is at the bottom.
air-bike.conseil2: Arms and legs work together: push the handle on the same side as the pushing leg.
air-bike.conseil3: Start at a pace you can hold, then speed up toward the end.

box-jumps.consigne: Swing your arms back, jump with both feet while swinging your arms forward, and land softly on the box, knees bent.
box-jumps.conseil1: Your arms drive the jump: back as you load, forward at takeoff.
box-jumps.conseil2: Land with your whole foot on the box, knees in line.
box-jumps.conseil3: Step down rather than jumping down.

burpees.legende4: Push-up: chest close to the floor
burpees.consigne: Hands on the floor, feet back, chest to the floor, then bring your feet in, stand up and jump with your arms up.
burpees.conseil1: Your body faces the same way throughout the movement.
burpees.conseil2: In the plank, body tight: no butt in the air.
burpees.conseil3: Light jump, soft landing on the balls of your feet.

clean-and-jerk.legende4: Bar in front of your knees
clean-and-jerk.consigne: Two parts: bring the bar up to your shoulders (clean), then dip your legs slightly and drive it overhead as you split your feet (jerk).
clean-and-jerk.conseil1: On the clean, bar close to your body and elbows forward on the catch.
clean-and-jerk.conseil2: For the jerk, your torso stays upright during the dip: your legs launch the bar.
clean-and-jerk.conseil3: In the split, arms locked, then bring your front and back feet together.

clean.legende2: Bar caught on your shoulders, elbows forward
clean.legende3: Bar in front of your knees
clean.legende5: Catch, elbows forward under the bar
clean.consigne: Bar close to your body: pull from the floor with your legs, then whip your elbows forward to catch it on the front of your shoulders.
clean.conseil1: Shoulder-width grip, back flat at the start.
clean.conseil2: The bar stays close to your body on the way up.
clean.conseil3: Catch with high elbows, bar resting on your collarbones.

course.consigne: Torso leaning slightly forward, land your foot under your hips and let your arms swing back and forth.
course.conseil1: Short, quick steps rather than long strides.
course.conseil3: Eyes ahead, not on your feet.

double-unders.legende2: In the air: the rope passes under your feet twice
double-unders.consigne: One jump, two turns of the rope: jump a little higher than a single under and spin the rope fast with your wrists.
double-unders.conseil1: Elbows close to your body, hands at hip height.
double-unders.conseil2: Your wrists turn the rope, not your arms.
double-unders.conseil3: Stay tight, legs almost straight, and land on your toes.

farmer-walk.consigne: A heavy weight in each hand, arms straight: walk with short steps, head up and chest open.
farmer-walk.conseil2: Chest open, shoulders down and back.
farmer-walk.conseil3: Abs tight, short and steady steps.

kettlebell-swings.consigne: A hip movement, not an arm movement: kettlebell between your legs, snap your hips forward to swing it to shoulder height.
kettlebell-swings.conseil1: Back flat, hips back as if closing a door with your butt.
kettlebell-swings.conseil2: Your arms stay straight: your glutes do the swinging.
kettlebell-swings.conseil3: At the top, body straight and tight, without leaning back.

power-clean.legende3: Bar in front of your knees
power-clean.consigne: Like a clean, but you catch the bar high: legs barely bent, without dropping into a full squat.
power-clean.conseil1: Back flat at the start, bar over mid-foot.
power-clean.conseil2: Drive hard through the floor and rise onto your toes before pulling with your arms.
power-clean.conseil3: Catch with hips above knees, elbows high and forward.

power-snatch.legende1: Bar on the floor, wide grip
power-snatch.legende3: Bar in front of your knees
power-snatch.consigne: Like a snatch, but you catch the bar with arms straight in a quarter squat, without dropping into a full squat.
power-snatch.conseil1: Wide grip: the bar sits in your hip crease when you’re standing.
power-snatch.conseil2: Bar close to your body, elbows high during the pull.
power-snatch.conseil3: Arms locked on the catch, then stand up.

rameur.legende2: Finish: legs straight, handle at your lower ribs
rameur.consigne: Push with your legs first, then swing your torso back and pull the handle to your lower ribs. On the way back, reverse the order: arms, torso, legs.
rameur.conseil1: Order matters: legs, torso, arms on the drive; arms, torso, legs on the recovery.
rameur.conseil3: The recovery is slower than the drive.

snatch.legende1: Bar on the floor, wide grip
snatch.legende3: Bar in front of your knees
snatch.legende6: The bar passes in front of your face
snatch.consigne: Very wide grip: rip the bar from the floor in one movement and catch it with arms straight overhead.
snatch.conseil1: A technical lift: learn it with a PVC pipe or an empty bar.
snatch.conseil2: Bar always close to your body on the way up.
snatch.conseil3: At the finish, arms locked, bar over the back of your neck.

thrusters.legende3: Squat, knees in line with your feet
thrusters.consigne: Bar resting on the front of your shoulders: squat down, then drive up and press the bar overhead in one movement.
thrusters.conseil1: Elbows high in front of you during the squat.
thrusters.conseil2: Knees in line with your feet, heels down.
thrusters.conseil3: Use the drive from your legs to press the bar.

wall-balls.consigne: Medicine ball against your chest: squat down, then drive up explosively and throw the ball to the target on the wall. Catch it and go again.
wall-balls.conseil1: Full squat on every rep, back straight.
wall-balls.conseil2: Your leg drive throws the ball; your arms finish the movement.
wall-balls.conseil3: Watch the target, catch the ball and drop straight back into the squat.

extension-lombaire.consigne: On the back extension bench, hips on the pad, feet anchored: lower your torso with a straight back, then come back up until you’re in line.
extension-lombaire.conseil1: The pad sits just below the top of your hips.
extension-lombaire.conseil2: Arms crossed over your chest, back straight.
extension-lombaire.conseil3: Come up until you’re in line, without arching beyond.

good-morning.consigne: Bar resting on your upper back and shoulders, knees slightly bent: hinge your torso forward keeping your back flat, then stand back up.
good-morning.conseil1: Start light: empty bar or a stick.
good-morning.conseil2: Back flat, knees slightly bent and fixed.
good-morning.conseil3: Go down until you feel the stretch in your hamstrings, no further.

rowing-barre.legende2: Bar to your belly button, elbows close to your body
rowing-barre.consigne: Torso leaning at 45°, back flat: row the bar to your belly button keeping your elbows close to your body, then lower it with arms straight.
rowing-barre.conseil1: Knees slightly bent, torso leaning at about 45°, back flat.
rowing-barre.conseil2: Elbows close to your body (about 45°), not flared.
rowing-barre.conseil3: Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top, lower without rounding your back.

rowing-haltere.consigne: One hand and one knee on the bench, back flat: row the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to your body, then lower it.
rowing-haltere.conseil1: Back flat, parallel to the floor.
rowing-haltere.conseil2: Drive your elbow toward your hip, not your shoulder.
rowing-haltere.conseil3: Your torso doesn’t twist during the movement.

rowing-machine.legende1: Arms straight, chest on the pad
rowing-machine.consigne: Seated, chest against the pad, handles in hand: pull your elbows back while squeezing your shoulder blades, then return with arms straight.
rowing-machine.conseil1: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
rowing-machine.conseil2: Your chest stays against the pad.
rowing-machine.conseil3: Elbows close to your body, squeeze your shoulder blades at the end.

rowing-t-bar.legende1: Bar between your legs, arms straight
rowing-t-bar.consigne: Standing over the bar, which runs between your legs: row the handle to your chest keeping your elbows close to your body, then lower it.
rowing-t-bar.conseil1: The bar runs between your legs, V-handle in your hands.
rowing-t-bar.conseil2: Torso leaning, back flat, knees slightly bent.

shrugs.consigne: Arms straight, weights in hand: raise your shoulders toward your ears, pause, then lower slowly.
shrugs.conseil1: Arms straight: your arms don’t do the pulling.
shrugs.conseil2: Go straight up toward your ears, without rolling your shoulders.

souleve-de-terre-roumain.consigne: Legs almost straight: push your hips back keeping your back flat, slide the bar down your thighs to just below your knees, then come back up.
souleve-de-terre-roumain.conseil2: Your hips move back: the bar slides down your thighs.
souleve-de-terre-roumain.conseil3: Stop when you feel the stretch in your hamstrings, back still flat.

souleve-de-terre-sumo.legende1: Bar on the floor, torso more upright
souleve-de-terre-sumo.legende2: Bar in front of your knees
souleve-de-terre-sumo.legende4: Very wide stance, hands between your knees
souleve-de-terre-sumo.consigne: Very wide stance, toes pointed out, hands between your knees: push your knees out and stand up keeping your back flat.
souleve-de-terre-sumo.conseil1: Feet much wider than your shoulders, toes pointed out.
souleve-de-terre-sumo.conseil2: Hands inside your knees, arms straight.
souleve-de-terre-sumo.conseil3: Knees in line with your feet, torso more upright than in a regular deadlift.

souleve-de-terre.legende1: Bar on the floor, back flat
souleve-de-terre.legende2: Bar in front of your knees
souleve-de-terre.consigne: Bar over mid-foot, back flat: push through the floor with your legs, keeping the bar against your legs, until you’re standing.
souleve-de-terre.conseil1: Feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot.
souleve-de-terre.conseil2: Back flat from start to finish, never rounded.
souleve-de-terre.conseil3: Bar against your legs all the way up.
souleve-de-terre.conseil4: At the top, squeeze your glutes without leaning back.

tirage-horizontal.consigne: Seated, feet on the platform, back straight: pull the handle to your stomach while squeezing your shoulder blades, without rocking back.
tirage-horizontal.conseil2: Elbows close to your body, handle toward your belly button.
tirage-horizontal.conseil3: Your torso stays almost still: your arms and back do the pulling.

tirage-vertical-prise-serree.consigne: Seated under the pulley, close-grip handle in hand: pull to your upper chest keeping your elbows close to your body, then let it back up.
tirage-vertical-prise-serree.conseil1: Hands close together on the V-handle.
tirage-vertical-prise-serree.conseil2: The pulley is above you, the cable comes straight down.
tirage-vertical-prise-serree.conseil3: Elbows at your sides, chest up.

tirage-vertical.consigne: Seated, thighs locked under the pads: pull the bar to your upper chest while squeezing your shoulder blades, then let it back up to straight arms.
tirage-vertical.conseil1: The pulley is right above you: the cable comes straight down.
tirage-vertical.conseil3: Drive your elbows down, not back.

developpe-arnold.legende1: Palms facing you, elbows in front
developpe-arnold.legende4: Arms open as your wrists rotate
developpe-arnold.consigne: Seated, dumbbells in front of your face, palms facing you: press up while rotating your wrists to finish palms forward, then lower while rotating back.
developpe-arnold.conseil1: Seated on a bench, backrest upright.
developpe-arnold.conseil2: At the bottom: palms facing you, elbows in front of your body.
developpe-arnold.conseil3: The rotation happens on the way up: palms forward at the top.

developpe-militaire.consigne: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward: press overhead without arching your back, then lower.
developpe-militaire.conseil1: Start: dumbbells at ear height, elbows under your wrists.
developpe-militaire.conseil2: Press until your arms are almost straight, without clanking the dumbbells.
developpe-militaire.conseil3: Abs and glutes tight: your back doesn’t arch.

elevations-frontales.legende1: Dumbbells in front of your thighs
elevations-frontales.legende2: Arms in front, at shoulder height
elevations-frontales.consigne: Dumbbells held horizontally in front of your thighs: raise your almost-straight arms in front of you to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
elevations-frontales.conseil2: Raise to eye height at most.
elevations-frontales.conseil3: No momentum: your torso doesn’t move.

elevations-laterales-a-la-poulie.legende1: Handle in front of the opposite hip
elevations-laterales-a-la-poulie.consigne: Low pulley beside you, handle held in the opposite hand: raise your arm out to the side until horizontal, then lower slowly.
elevations-laterales-a-la-poulie.conseil1: The cable runs in front of your body.
elevations-laterales-a-la-poulie.conseil2: Arm almost straight, raise it to horizontal.
elevations-laterales-a-la-poulie.conseil3: Do all the reps on one side, then switch.

elevations-laterales.legende2: Arms horizontal out to the sides
elevations-laterales.consigne: Arms almost straight: raise the dumbbells out to the sides until horizontal, without shrugging, then lower slowly.
elevations-laterales.conseil3: Shoulders down: your traps aren’t doing the work.

face-pull.legende2: Rope to your face, elbows high
face-pull.legende3: Elbows high and wide, hands at your face
face-pull.consigne: Pulley at face height, rope in hand: pull toward your eyes while spreading your hands, elbows high, then return to straight arms.
face-pull.conseil1: Elbows at shoulder height or higher.
face-pull.conseil2: Spread your hands to either side of your head at the end of the movement.

oiseau-arriere-d-epaule.legende1: Seated and bent over, arms hanging
oiseau-arriere-d-epaule.consigne: Seated at the end of a bench, torso bent forward over your thighs, back flat: open your arms out to the sides until horizontal, then lower.
oiseau-arriere-d-epaule.conseil1: Torso bent almost onto your thighs (or chest-supported on an incline bench).

push-press.consigne: Bar on the front of your shoulders: dip your knees slightly, then drive with your legs and finish with your arms to bring the bar overhead.
push-press.conseil2: Your leg drive launches the bar, your arms finish it.
push-press.conseil3: Arms locked at the top, bar over the back of your neck.

rowing-menton.legende2: Bar under your chin, elbows high
rowing-menton.consigne: Bar against your thighs: pull it up along your body by raising your elbows out to the sides, up to your lower chest, then lower.
rowing-menton.conseil2: Your elbows rise higher than your hands.

communs-jambes.conseil1: Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
communs-jambes.conseil2: Knees in line with your feet: they don’t cave in or flare out.
communs-jambes.conseil3: Go down at least until your thighs are parallel to the floor, back straight, heels down.
communs-jambes.conseil4: Push through your heels to stand up.

abducteurs-machine.consigne: Seated, pads against the outside of your knees: push your legs apart, then bring them back slowly.
abducteurs-machine.conseil1: Back against the backrest, hands on the handles.
abducteurs-machine.conseil2: Push out smoothly, hold for 1 second, return slowly.

fentes-bulgares.consigne: Top of your back foot on a bench: lower your back knee toward the floor, front knee over your ankle, then come back up.
fentes-bulgares.conseil1: Bench at knee height, top of your back foot resting on it.
fentes-bulgares.conseil2: Front foot far enough from the bench to keep your knee over your ankle.

fentes.consigne: Big step forward: lower your back knee close to the floor, front knee over your ankle, come back up, then switch legs.
fentes.conseil2: Front knee over your ankle, in line with your foot.
fentes.conseil3: Torso upright, back knee just brushing the floor.

front-squat.legende1: Bar on the front of your shoulders
front-squat.legende3: Bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high
front-squat.legende4: Knees in line with your feet
front-squat.consigne: Bar resting in front, on top of your shoulders and collarbones, elbows high: squat down keeping your torso upright, then stand up.
front-squat.conseil1: The bar rests on the front of your shoulders, against your throat, not in your hands.
front-squat.conseil2: Elbows high and pointing forward all the way down.
front-squat.conseil3: Knees in line with your feet, torso more upright than in a back squat.

hack-squat.consigne: Back against the backrest, shoulders under the pads, feet on the platform: lower the sled by bending your knees, then push.
hack-squat.conseil1: Back and hips against the backrest.
hack-squat.conseil2: Feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
hack-squat.conseil3: Don’t lock your knees at the top.

hip-thrust.consigne: Upper back on a bench, bar across your hips, feet flat: drive your hips up while squeezing your glutes, then lower.
hip-thrust.conseil1: The bottom of your shoulder blades on the edge of a bench.
hip-thrust.conseil2: Bar in your hip crease, with a pad.
hip-thrust.conseil3: At the top, shins vertical and body flat like a table.
hip-thrust.conseil4: Chin tucked, eyes toward your knees.

leg-curl.consigne: Lying face down, pad behind your ankles: curl your heels toward your glutes, then lower slowly.
leg-curl.conseil1: Hips against the bench throughout the movement.
leg-curl.conseil3: Lower slowly, without dropping the weight.

leg-extension.consigne: Back against the backrest, pad on your lower shins: straighten your legs fully, then lower under control.
leg-extension.conseil1: Adjust the backrest so your knees are at the edge of the seat.
leg-extension.conseil2: Pad resting on your lower shins.
leg-extension.conseil3: Hold the handles and keep your butt on the seat.

mollets-assis.consigne: Seated, pad on your knees, balls of your feet on the step: raise your heels as high as you can, then lower them slowly.
mollets-assis.conseil1: Only the balls of your feet are on the step, heels hanging off.
mollets-assis.conseil2: Pad snug on your lower thighs.
mollets-assis.conseil3: Slow movement, pause at the top.

mollets-debout.consigne: Balls of your feet on the edge of a step, heels hanging off: rise onto your toes as high as you can, then lower slowly.
mollets-debout.conseil1: Only the balls of your feet are on the step.
mollets-debout.conseil2: Drop your heels below the step before rising again.
mollets-debout.conseil3: Hold on to something for balance.

overhead-squat.consigne: Bar locked out overhead, wide grip: squat down while keeping the bar stacked over mid-foot.
overhead-squat.conseil1: Wide grip, elbows locked and shoulders active (push the bar toward the ceiling).
overhead-squat.conseil2: Torso as upright as possible, eyes forward.
overhead-squat.conseil3: Start with a PVC pipe or an empty bar: it's as much a mobility move as a strength one.

pistol-squat.legende1: On one leg, the other in front
pistol-squat.legende2: Lowering on one leg, the other straight
pistol-squat.consigne: On one leg, the other straight out in front: lower as far as you can with your heel down, then stand back up.
pistol-squat.conseil1: Arms straight out in front for balance.
pistol-squat.conseil2: Standing-leg heel down, knee tracking over your foot.
pistol-squat.conseil3: To learn it: lower onto a bench or hold on to something.

pont-fessier.legende1: Lying down, shoulders on the floor
pont-fessier.consigne: Lying on your back, shoulders on the floor, feet flat: drive your hips up while squeezing your glutes, then lower.
pont-fessier.conseil1: Shoulders and head stay on the floor (no bench, unlike the hip thrust).
pont-fessier.conseil2: Feet flat, heels close to your butt.
pont-fessier.conseil3: At the top, knees, hips and shoulders in line; squeeze your glutes for 1 second.

presse-a-cuisses.consigne: Back and hips pressed into the seat, feet on the platform: push without locking your knees, then lower slowly.
presse-a-cuisses.conseil1: Feet hip-width apart in the middle of the platform.
presse-a-cuisses.conseil2: Lower until your knees reach 90°, without your hips lifting off.
presse-a-cuisses.conseil3: Don't lock your knees at the top.

squat-goblet.consigne: Dumbbell held with both hands against your chest: squat down between your knees with your torso upright and knees tracking over your feet, then stand up.
squat-goblet.conseil1: Dumbbell held vertically against your chest, elbows down.
squat-goblet.conseil2: Feet slightly wider than your shoulders, knees tracking over your feet.
squat-goblet.conseil3: At the bottom, your elbows go between your knees.

squat.legende1: Standing, bar on your upper back
squat.consigne: Bar on your upper back, back straight: sit your hips down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, knees tracking over your feet, then drive through your heels.

squats-poids-du-corps.consigne: Arms out in front for balance: sit your hips down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, knees tracking over your feet, heels down, then stand up.

step-up.consigne: Place your whole foot on the box: drive through that foot until you're standing tall over that knee, then step down under control.
step-up.conseil1: Box around knee height, whole foot on it.
step-up.conseil2: Drive through the heel of the foot on the box, without pushing off the other leg.
step-up.conseil3: Stand all the way up, then lower slowly.

communs-pectoraux.conseil1: Feet flat on the floor, butt and shoulder blades pressed into the bench.
communs-pectoraux.conseil2: Elbows at about 45° from your torso, not flared out to 90°.
communs-pectoraux.conseil3: At the bottom, forearms vertical and elbows at a right angle (90°).
communs-pectoraux.conseil4: Beginner: start with just the bar and use a spotter.

developpe-couche-halteres.consigne: Lying on a flat bench, a dumbbell in each hand: lower them to the sides of your chest, then press up.
developpe-couche-halteres.conseil1: Flat bench, feet planted on the floor.
developpe-couche-halteres.conseil2: Start with arms straight, palms facing your feet.
developpe-couche-halteres.conseil3: Lower until your elbows reach 90°, elbows at about 45° from your torso.
developpe-couche-halteres.conseil4: Press back up bringing the dumbbells together, without clanking them.

developpe-couche-prise-serree.legende1: Bar at lower chest, elbows tucked
developpe-couche-prise-serree.consigne: Hands shoulder-width apart on the bar: lower it to your lower chest keeping your elbows tucked, then press.
developpe-couche-prise-serree.conseil2: Elbows close to your body on the way down.

developpe-couche.consigne: Lying on a flat bench, shoulder blades squeezed, feet on the floor: lower the bar to your lower chest, then press up.

developpe-decline.consigne: On a decline bench, feet hooked under the pads: lower the bar to your lower chest, then press up.
developpe-decline.conseil1: Head lower than your hips (15–30°), feet hooked.
developpe-decline.conseil2: Bar lowered to your lower chest.
developpe-decline.conseil3: Get a spotter to help you unrack and rack the bar.

developpe-incline-halteres.consigne: On a bench inclined to 30–45°, a dumbbell in each hand: lower them to your upper chest, then press up.
developpe-incline-halteres.conseil2: Palms facing your feet, elbows at about 45° from your torso.
developpe-incline-halteres.conseil3: Lower until your elbows reach 90°, press back up bringing the dumbbells together.

developpe-incline.consigne: On a bench inclined to 30–45°: lower the bar to your upper chest, then press up.
developpe-incline.conseil2: Bar lowered to your upper chest, just below the collarbones.
developpe-incline.conseil3: Elbows at about 45° from your torso; at the bottom, elbows at 90°.

ecarte-halteres.consigne: Lying down, elbows slightly bent: open your arms out to the sides without going below the bench, then bring them back together over your chest.
ecarte-halteres.conseil2: Open until you feel a stretch in your chest, no lower than the bench.
ecarte-halteres.conseil3: Close as if you were hugging a tree trunk.

ecarte-poulie-basse.legende1: Arms open toward the low pulleys
ecarte-poulie-basse.legende4: Hands in front of your face
ecarte-poulie-basse.consigne: Pulleys set low: bring your hands up and forward until they meet at chin height. Targets the upper chest.
ecarte-poulie-basse.conseil1: Torso upright, one foot in front of the other.
ecarte-poulie-basse.conseil2: Elbows slightly bent, move in an arc.

ecarte-poulie-haute.legende1: Arms open toward the high pulleys
ecarte-poulie-haute.legende2: Hands meeting in front of your hips
ecarte-poulie-haute.legende4: Hands in front of your hips
ecarte-poulie-haute.consigne: Pulleys set high: bring your hands down and forward until they meet in front of your hips. Targets the lower chest.
ecarte-poulie-haute.conseil1: One foot in front of the other, torso leaning slightly forward.

ecarte-poulie-moyenne.legende2: Hands meeting in front of your chest
ecarte-poulie-moyenne.legende4: Hands in front of your chest
ecarte-poulie-moyenne.consigne: Pulleys at shoulder height: bring your hands together in front of your chest, keeping your arms horizontal. Targets the middle chest.
ecarte-poulie-moyenne.conseil1: Arms at shoulder height throughout the movement.

pec-deck-butterfly.consigne: Seated on the machine, back flat against the pad, forearms against the pads: bring your arms together in front of you until the pads touch, then open slowly.
pec-deck-butterfly.conseil1: Adjust the seat so your elbows are at shoulder height.
pec-deck-butterfly.conseil2: Arms bent at 90° against the pads.
pec-deck-butterfly.conseil3: Open slowly without going too far back.

presse-pectoraux.consigne: Seated on the machine, back flat against the pad, handles at chest height: press forward without locking your elbows, then return slowly.
presse-pectoraux.conseil1: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height.
presse-pectoraux.conseil2: Back and head against the backrest.
presse-pectoraux.conseil3: Press until your arms are almost straight.

pull-over.consigne: Lying down, a dumbbell held with both hands, arms almost straight: lower it behind your head, then bring it back over your chest.
pull-over.conseil2: Lower until you feel a stretch, with no shoulder pain.
pull-over.conseil3: Hips and lower back stay on the bench.

conditions.corps:
By creating an account, you agree to these rules. They're here to keep the app a friendly, safe place for everyone.

1. The app

AS Sport is a free app to log your workouts, track your progress and share with your friends. It is provided “as is”: the publisher does their best to keep it running smoothly, but cannot guarantee it will always be available or error-free.

2. Your account

  • You must be at least 15 years old (or have a parent’s consent).
  • One account per person. You are responsible for what is done with your account: keep your password to yourself.
  • Choose an appropriate username and photo: other users can see them.

3. Community rules

Zero tolerance for abusive content or behavior. You may not post (username, photo, message, comment, challenge name…):

  • insults, harassment, threats or body shaming;
  • hateful, racist, sexist, homophobic or discriminatory content;
  • sexual, violent or shocking content;
  • scams, advertising, spam or dangerous links;
  • promotion of performance-enhancing drugs or practices that are dangerous to health;
  • someone else’s personal information without their consent;
  • any illegal content or content that doesn’t belong to you.

4. Reporting and blocking

You can report a message, a conversation, a comment, a profile or a challenge, and block someone at any time. Reports are reviewed by the publisher, usually within 24 hours. The content in question may be removed and its author suspended from social features or banned, without notice.

5. Your content

You keep ownership of what you post. You simply allow the app to store it and show it to the people you share it with (your friends, challenge participants). You can delete your workouts and your account at any time.

6. Health

The app does not replace the advice of a doctor or a certified coach. Programs, workout ideas and tips are for guidance only: adapt them to your level, warm up, and stop if you feel pain. You train at your own risk.

7. Ownership of the app

The name, design, texts and code of AS Sport belong to its publisher. All rights reserved: you may not copy, reproduce or republish them without permission.

8. Personal data

Everything is explained in the privacy policy.

9. Changes and contact

These terms may change; if there is a significant change, you will be notified in the app. For any question: the app’s Contact page. These terms are governed by French law.

confidentialite.corps:
This page explains, in plain words, what data the app stores, why, who can see it and how to delete it. The app is free, ad-free, and your data is never sold.

1. Who is responsible for your data?

The publisher of AS Sport. For any question or request, write to them from the app’s Contact page: your message goes straight to them.

2. Data stored

  • Your account: email address and password (the password is encrypted by Google Firebase; nobody can read it, not even the publisher).
  • Your profile: username (required) and, if you choose, first name, last name, age, height, weight, goal and profile photo.
  • Your workouts: sessions, exercises, sets, weights, running times, how you felt, notes, records, routines, current program and workout photos.
  • Your nutrition: supplements and creatine intake.
  • The social side: your friends, your private messages, your reactions, your comments, your challenges and the reports you send.
  • Messages sent from the Contact page.
  • A few usage statistics: date of your last visit, number of visits, number of workouts (for running the app).

The app does not collect your location, your contacts or your Apple Health data, and uses no advertising trackers.

3. Why?

  • To make the app work: save your workouts, calculate your records and progress, and sync across all your devices.
  • For the friend features you choose to use.
  • For safety and moderation: handling reports and blocking abuse.
  • To reply to your messages and improve the app.

Legal basis: performance of the service you request by creating an account, and the publisher’s legitimate interest in keeping the app secure.

4. Who can see your data?

  • You, on all your devices.
  • Any signed-in user can find your username, friend code, profile photo and goal by searching for you, in order to add you as a friend.
  • Your accepted friends see your workouts (if sharing is on; you can turn it off in Friends), your records, your stats, and the reactions and comments on your workouts. Your workout photos stay private.
  • Challenge participants see your username and your score in that challenge.
  • The publisher (administrator) can see profiles, workouts and statistics for support and moderation, as well as reported content. They do not read your private messages, except those reported to them.

5. Where is it stored?

With Google Firebase (Google Cloud), which hosts the database and accounts. Servers may be located outside the European Union; Google covers these transfers with the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts. A copy of your data is also kept on your phone so the app works offline.

6. How long?

As long as your account exists. When you delete it, your profile, workouts, nutrition, photos, routines, the reactions and comments you received and your friendships are erased immediately. Messages and comments you wrote on your friends’ content remain visible to them; ask for their deletion via the Contact page if you wish. Reports are deleted once handled.

7. Your rights

  • Access and download your data: Profile › “Download my data”.
  • Correct it: Profile › “Edit”.
  • Erase it: Profile › “Delete my account and data”, or delete a workout at any time.
  • Stop sharing your workouts with your friends: Friends › “My workouts are shared”.
  • For any other request (objection, restriction…), write from the Contact page. You can also contact the French data protection authority, the CNIL (cnil.fr).

8. Minimum age

The app is intended for people aged 15 and over. Below that age, a parent’s consent is required.

9. Security

Connections are encrypted (HTTPS). Security rules prevent anyone from reading or changing another user’s data without permission. Keep your password to yourself.

10. Changes

If this policy changes, the date at the top of the page is updated and, if the change is significant, you will be notified in the app.
